title: Discover and instrument your application services

blocks.content: Instrumentation Hub discovers the application services running on your cluster and lets you instrument them without code changes. This guide follows the **Install Alloy on Kubernetes for Instrumentation Hub** guide: it assumes your collectors are installed and active, so discovered services are already flowing in. To begin, open the Instrumentation Hub landing page.
Go to the **Instrumentation Hub** landing page.
blocks.tooltip: Start here to see what has been discovered on your stack.

blocks.description: A stack with no clusters redirects to the onboarding page, where there is nothing to instrument; a stack with clusters shows the landing page with the Application instrumentation card.

whenTrue.content: This stack hasn't reported any Kubernetes clusters yet, so there are no discovered services to instrument. Install a collector first — the install guide opens in this sidebar.

blocks.content: Open the **Install Alloy on Kubernetes for Instrumentation Hub** guide and follow it to install Alloy on a cluster.
blocks.tooltip: Opens the collector installation guide for this stack.

whenTrue.content: Once Alloy is installed and the Instrumentation Hub landing page shows discovered services, reopen this guide to continue.

whenFalse.content: You're on the Instrumentation Hub landing page, which shows what has been discovered and how much of it is instrumented.
Next, open the application services view and choose the services you want to instrument.

blocks.content: On the **Application instrumentation** card, click **View & instrument services**.
blocks.tooltip: Opens the list of services discovered on your clusters.

blocks.content:
Select a cluster from the list on the left, then choose what to instrument: click **Select all** for every service in the cluster, select the checkbox next to a namespace, or click a namespace name and select individual services. Choose these yourself — instrumentation changes what is monitored on your stack.

SDK injection covers .NET, Java, Node.js, and Python services. You can select services written in other languages, but they're instrumented with eBPF only.
blocks.tooltip: Pick the clusters, namespaces, or individual services you want to instrument.

blocks.content: Click **Instrument services**. It's only available when your selection includes at least one service that isn't already instrumented.
blocks.tooltip: Continues to a review of your selection before anything changes.

whenFalse.content: You chose the services to instrument and opened the review flow — nothing has changed on your cluster yet.

Now review your selection, check the pipeline settings, and start instrumentation. If you haven't activated Application Observability on this stack, you're prompted to activate it before you can continue; activation allows use of the product and begins host-hours billing.

blocks.content: Confirm your selection on the **Review Selection** page, then click **Continue**.
blocks.tooltip: Moves on to the pipeline settings for the affected namespaces.

blocks.content:
Review the settings on the **Pipeline Configuration** page. R.E.D metrics and service-to-service links are included. Switch on any optional settings you want, such as **Ongoing instrumentation**, **Traces**, **Application logs**, or **Profiling**.

These settings apply to the whole namespace: every instrumented service in the selected namespaces is updated to match, not only the services you add in this run.
blocks.tooltip: These settings apply to every instrumented service in the selected namespaces.

blocks.content: Click **Instrument now**. The services you instrument restart, because the OpenTelemetry SDK can only load into a process as it starts. For replicated workloads this is a rolling replacement rather than downtime.
blocks.tooltip: Starts instrumentation; the affected services restart to load the SDK.

blocks.content: Watch the services list: the services you selected show a pending instrumentation status, then change to instrumented as the change rolls out. Instrumentation can take a few minutes, depending on how much you chose to instrument.
blocks.tooltip: Your selected services move from pending to instrumented as the change rolls out.

whenFalse.content: You instrumented your selected application services. Success looks like each service you selected showing a pending status in the services table, then switching to instrumented as the rollout completes.
